@about: Roller chain sprockets add-on (0.9 SU.961). Words of the add-on only; English only.
cmd.chains.help: List the roller-chain table: chain numbers with pitch, roller diameter, inner width and plate height, and how many catalogues agree.
cmd.chainsources.help: Show the public catalogues the chain dimensions were read from.
cmd.sprocket.help: Draw a roller-chain sprocket for a chain number and a tooth count: tooth outline, pitch circle, centre lines and bore.
chains.head: Roller chains: {n} rows. Millimetres. p = pitch, d1 = roller (bushing for 25 and 35) diameter, b1 = width between inner plates, h2 = inner plate height.
chains.agree: at least {n} catalogues agree on p, d1, b1
chains.foot: Read from public catalogues, kept where two agree; not copied from ISO 606 or ASME B29.1. CHAINSOURCES lists them.
src.head: Catalogues the chain table was read from (fetched {date}):
src.not_standard: These are manufacturers' and reference pages. We do not hold ISO 606 or ANSI/ASME B29.1 and nothing here is copied from them.
err.chain: No chain {name} in the table. Type CHAINS to see the chain numbers that are there.
err.teeth: A sprocket needs a whole number of teeth, at least 6.
err.bore: The bore must be at least 0 and clear the root circle.
done: Sprocket for chain {chain}, {n} teeth: pitch diameter {D}, root diameter {Df}, tip diameter {Dt} mm.
mesh.ok: Checked against the chain it is made for: the rollers seat and clear the outline by at least {gap} mm.
mesh.bad: Check failed: the chain does not seat cleanly on this tooth count. Try more teeth.
note.tooth: The tooth form is this add-on's own (seat clearance {c} %, seat half angle {beta} degrees, tip {tip} p above the pitch circle), not the standard's tooth form. Check it against your sprocket supplier before cutting.
note.noplate: The plate height of this chain is not agreed by two catalogues and is left out; it is not used for the outline.
